claims.text: Its contents page, as released: 'Concepts for Antigravity Within Newtonian Physics', 'Negating Newtonian Gravity', 'Energy Estimate for Newtonian Levitation', 'Concepts for Antigravity Within General Relativity', 'Antigravity via Gravitomagnetic Forces', 'Forward's Dipole Gravitational Field Generator', 'Felber's Relativistic Antigravity Effect', 'Negative Energy-Induced Antigravity', 'Cosmological Antigravity', 'Pressure as a Source of Gravity', 'Vacuum Energy of Einstein's Cosmological Constant', 'Dark Energy', 'Antigravity Propulsion Application of Dark/Vacuum Energy', 'Quantum Antigravity Propulsion Concepts', 'Antigravity via Quantum Vacuum Zero-Point Fluctuation Force', 'Antigravity via Nonretarded Quantum Interatomic Dispersion Force', 'Conclusion: The Way Forward', with appendices on static radial fields, squeezed quantum vacuum, gravitationally squeezed electromagnetic zero-point fluctuations and the dynamical Casimir effect.

claims.sourceText: Defense Intelligence Reference Document DIA-08-1003-018, 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications', 30 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, 45 pages as released, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_19-DIRD_Antigravity_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: Its conclusion, 'The Way Forward', verbatim in part: 'This report has reviewed and analyzed a number of antigravity concepts that are found within Newtonian gravity theory, General Relativity Theory, semi-classical quantum gravity theory, quantum field theory, and nonretarded quantum interatomic dispersion force theory. One found that plausible mechanisms exist within Newtonian and general relativistic theories whereby one could embody a realistic device that produces a significant antigravity force. However, one discovered that there are daunting technical challenges that arise in each of the proposed embodiments.'
Cover page reads "30 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1003-018", series "Acquisition Threat Support".

claims.sourceText: Defense Intelligence Reference Document DIA-08-1003-018, 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications', 30 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, 45 pages as released, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_19-DIRD_Antigravity_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: And: 'Antigravity forces produced by quantum electromagnetic vacuum ZPF or by nonretarded quantum interatomic dispersion forces in a curved spacetime (that is, gravitational field) are very feeble, but there are proposals based on other theoretical and empirical studies which suggest that these forces can be amplified to macroscopic level. However, there are a number of difficult technical challenges to overcome in order to achieve success.' Its first named next step is that 'Presently, the technology does not exist to achieve the astronomical mass densities, extreme velocities or accelerations of mass motion, and the large device dimensions required to produce large enough antigravity forces for useful propulsion'.

claims.text: THE ZERO-COUNTS, taken over the whole released 45-page PDF on 19 September 2026: Biefeld 0, electrogravitics 0, ion wind 0, Podkletnov 0, and THOMAS TOWNSEND BROWN ABSENT. The three occurrences of 'Brown' are other authors' surnames in the reference list. Alcubierre occurs once, as reference [43], the 1994 Classical and Quantum Gravity citation, and that is its only appearance in this document. A count is checkable and an adjective is not, which is why the node carries numbers.

claims.text: WHAT HIS ANTIGRAVITY SURVEY ACTUALLY COVERS, from the released contents page of DIA-08-1003-018: antigravity within Newtonian physics, an energy estimate for Newtonian levitation, antigravity via gravitomagnetic forces, Forward's dipole gravitational field generator, Felber's relativistic antigravity effect, negative energy-induced antigravity, cosmological antigravity, the vacuum energy of Einstein's cosmological constant, dark energy, and quantum antigravity propulsion concepts via zero-point fluctuation force and nonretarded interatomic dispersion force. It is a survey of theoretical routes within accepted physics, with appendices on the Casimir effect and squeezed vacuum.

claims.sourceText: Defense Intelligence Reference Document DIA-08-1003-018, 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications', 30 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, 'Acquisition Threat Support', 45 pages as released, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_19-DIRD_Antigravity_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: HIS OWN CONCLUSION, verbatim: 'One found that plausible mechanisms exist within Newtonian and general relativistic theories whereby one could embody a realistic device that produces a significant antigravity force. However, one discovered that there are daunting technical challenges that arise in each of the proposed embodiments. Mechanical embodiments that produce antigravity forces require kilometer-sized apparatus, astronomical-sized masses and densities, or extreme mass velocities and accelerations.' And: 'Negative energy has been produced in the lab in very small quantities. The technologies used for producing negative energy are nascent, and so it will be some time before it can be ascertained whether they are capable of producing the astronomical amounts of negative energy required to generate significant antigravity forces.'

claims.text: THE MOST CHECKABLE FINDING THE PROPULSION STRAND PRODUCED, AND IT IS ABOUT THIS SERIES. DIRD DIA-08-1003-018, 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications', cover-dated 30 March 2010 under the 'Acquisition Threat Support' banner, 45 pages as released, attributed on the DIA list of 9 January 2018 to Dr Eric Davis of EarthTech International, DOES NOT MENTION THOMAS TOWNSEND BROWN. Word counts over the whole released PDF, taken 19 September 2026: Biefeld 0, electrogravitics 0, Podkletnov 0. 'Brown' occurs three times and every one of them is the surname of a different author in the reference list: L. S. Brown and Maclay, 'Vacuum Stress between Conducting Plates', Physical Review 184 (1969); H. R. Brown as co-editor of 'The Philosophy of Vacuum' (1991); and J. H. Brownell on Casimir photons (2008). Alcubierre occurs once, as reference [43].

claims.sourceText: Defense Intelligence Reference Document DIA-08-1003-018, 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications', 30 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, 45 pages as released, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_19-DIRD_Antigravity_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: WHAT THE ZERO-COUNTS ARE AND ARE NOT EVIDENCE FOR, stated so no later session overstates them. THEY ARE EVIDENCE that the United States government's own commissioned survey of antigravity for aerospace applications, written under the same programme this board maps, is a review of gravitomagnetic forces, Forward's dipole generator, Felber's effect, negative energy, dark energy, the cosmological constant and quantum vacuum zero-point fluctuation force, and that it never reaches for the figure the electrogravitics literature treats as its origin. THEY ARE NOT EVIDENCE that DIA considered Brown and rejected him: the document shows no sign of having considered him at all, and an absence is not an adjudication. THEY ARE NOT EVIDENCE that Brown's work was suppressed, hidden or classified; nothing opened supports that and nothing here asserts it.

Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program' - the redaction between them is (b)(3):10 USC 424. Verified by downloading this DIRD and scanning its full text on 23 August 2026. The scans are OCR-degraded, so the quotation is normalised from the damaged rendering.

edges.note: EarthTech International supplied six of the 38 DIRDs through Eric Davis plus one through Hal Puthoff, making it the single most represented institution on the author list.

edges.label: The government's own 45-page antigravity survey does not mention Brown at all
edges.note: THE ABSENCE EDGE, AND THIS NOTE IS WHAT KEEPS IT HONEST. Word counts over the whole released PDF, taken 19 September 2026: Biefeld 0, electrogravitics 0, ion wind 0, Podkletnov 0; 'Brown' occurs three times and all three are other authors' surnames in the reference list (L. S. Brown and Maclay 1969, H. R. Brown as co-editor of 'The Philosophy of Vacuum', J. H. Brownell 2008). WHAT THIS IS: a Tier 1 fact about a named, dated, openable document, checkable in 45 pages. WHAT THIS IS NOT: a finding that DIA considered Brown and rejected him, because the document shows no sign of having considered him. NOBODY DENIED ANYTHING, which is why the verdict is association and not directed, and the edge must never be rendered or summarised as 'DIA rejected Brown'.
